newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures down in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures down in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures drifted lower by midday on Tuesday in line with softer Japanese prices and in the absence of news which may perk up the market, dealers said.

"It was flat and the level of activity this morning was zero. Prices were marked down after the Japanese prices came off and the situation this afternoon doesn't look promising," a local rubber trader said.
Prices of Tokyo's benchmark February contract shed two yen to 138.6 in the morning session. Kobe's February contact fell 1.1 yen to 138.9.
"It's a very soft market. There simply is no news which can lift trading today," another dealer said.
At 0445 GMT, November RSS3 was indicated at 127.25-129.25 U.S. cents a kg from 129.25 cents.
November RSS1 was indicated at 182.50-184.50 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.31) a kg from Monday's settlement of 185.50 cents.
November TSR20 was indicated at 177.00-179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg against the previous 179.50 cents.
